questions.q: How long does the International Space Station take to go once around the Earth?
questions.do: Click the ISS dot on the map (or type ISS in Find a satellite) and read Once round the Earth. Check it against the Checks table.
questions.a: About 93 minutes (the lab shows about 92.9 min). The ISS orbits only about 400 km up, so it goes round fast.

questions.q: Compare the ISS with the NavIC satellite NVS-01. How long does each take to go once around, and what does that mean for someone in India?
questions.do: Click NavIC under Show and select NVS-01 (IRNSS-1J). Read Once round the Earth and the pass table in When can I see it? Then compare with the ISS.
questions.a: ISS: about 93 minutes. NVS-01: about 24 hours (23.94 h). NVS-01 goes round once a day, so from India it stays at almost the same spot in the sky, over the Indian Ocean at about 129.5°E.

questions.q: Can you see Hubble from London? Compare with Delhi.
questions.do: Type HST in Find a satellite. In When can I see it? set Your place to London, then to Delhi, and look at the pass table each time.
questions.a: From London: no passes higher than 10°. From Delhi it does pass. Hubble's orbit tilt is only about 28.5°, so it is never seen from far north or far south of the tropics.

questions.q: Why can you see the space station only just after sunset or just before sunrise?
questions.do: Read the note under the pass table in When can I see it? and the In sunlight now line for the ISS.
questions.a: A pass is visible only when the satellite is in sunlight while your sky is dark. That happens just after sunset or before sunrise. In daytime the sky is too bright; late at night the station is in Earth's shadow.

questions.q: What went wrong with India's NVS-02 satellite in 2025, and what orbit is it stuck in?
questions.do: Select NVS-02 (IRNSS-1K) and read the note under its details. Then find the NVS-02 row in the Checks table.
questions.a: Its engine valve failed in 2025, so it never reached its circular orbit. It is stuck in a stretched orbit between about 210 km and 37,245 km high.
